# Verification Manual

<!-- Generated by tools/verification_manual.py. Do not edit by hand:
     run `python tools/verification_manual.py --write` instead. -->

Each case below is a small model built with the public `core` API and solved
by the same `OpenSeesRunner` the application uses. The computed values are
compared with a closed-form or published reference; the relative error must
stay within the tolerance shown. CI regenerates this file and fails when a
tolerance is exceeded or the file is out of date
(`tests/integration/test_verification_manual.py`).

Units are SI (m, N, kg, s) for the V cases and kip-inch for the D (design)
cases, as in the AISC examples. Errors below 1e-6 are floating-point noise
and are printed as `< 1e-6`.

**20 of 20 cases pass.**

## V-01 — Cantilever with a tip load

**Model.** 2D cantilever, L = 4 m, one elastic beam-column; P = 10 kN down at the tip.

**Reference.** Euler-Bernoulli beam theory: δ = PL³/3EI, θ = PL²/2EI.

| Quantity | Unit | OpenSees Studio | Reference | Rel. error | Tolerance | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tip deflection | m | 0.0133333 | 0.0133333 | < 1e-06 | 1e-09 | ✅ |
| Tip rotation | rad | 0.005 | 0.005 | < 1e-06 | 1e-09 | ✅ |
| Base shear | N | 10000 | 10000 | < 1e-06 | 1e-09 | ✅ |
| Base moment | N·m | 40000 | 40000 | < 1e-06 | 1e-09 | ✅ |

## V-15 — Plastic moment of a rectangle

**Model.** 2D cantilever column, L = 3 m, one force-based element with a 60-fibre 0.3 × 0.5 m elastic-perfectly-plastic section, pushed to 8 yield displacements. Beyond about 10, the fully yielded section has no tangent stiffness and OpenSees' force-based element no longer converges its section state: give a perfectly plastic material a little hardening for large drifts.

**Reference.** Mp = fy·b·h²/4.

| Quantity | Unit | OpenSees Studio | Reference | Rel. error | Tolerance | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Base moment at 8 yield drifts (fy b h² / 4) | N·m | 4.68613e+06 | 4.6875e+06 | 2.9e-04 | 1e-03 | ✅ |
